approval_required_for: Any adoption or change of numeric precision, quantization policy, tolerance policy, or approximation behavior.
Any architecture-level selection of pipeline stages, tile sizes, parallelism, memory layout, data packing, buffering policy, or scheduling policy derived from prepared inputs.
Any AXI/DDR access policy, memory-interface assumption, bandwidth allocation, or board-level deployment constraint that becomes part of the design.
Any major template, backend, toolchain, or code-generation strategy change based on these materials.
Any design-space pruning that removes viable architecture candidates or encodes an unapproved architecture decision.
expected_evidence: Executable stage log showing successful parsing of task_spec, model_config, board materials, quantization materials, and tool materials.
Manifest listing source paths, versions, timestamps or hashes for all prepared inputs.
Parsed model evidence including layer count, hidden size, intermediate size, vocabulary size, RoPE/config fields, norm semantics, Q head count, KV head count, and tensor-shape derivations.
Explicit evidence that GQA metadata is preserved and not normalized into MHA assumptions.
Numeric/quantization evidence showing imported policies, precisions, scales or calibration references, and whether they are candidates versus approved constraints.
Board evidence including resource limits, memory capacity/bandwidth assumptions, AXI/DDR interface parameters, clocks, and backend target constraints.
Template/design-space evidence showing candidate parameters and bounds without claiming final selection.
Evidence that no tests, golden outputs, tolerance settings, or checker files were modified.
Run-directory artifact inventory suitable for downstream checker stages.
decision.reason: The requested stage prepares and records model, numeric, template, design-space, board, quantization, and tool inputs. It is an input/evidence preparation stage and does not by itself delete tests, alter golden outputs, loosen tolerances, bypass checkers, or claim a design pass. It is safe to run, with later checker stages required to validate consistency and any architecture-level choices requiring recorded approval before adoption.
risks: Input materials may be stale, incomplete, or inconsistent across task spec, model config, board, quantization, and tool directories.
Incorrect parsing could change model semantics or tensor shapes before later validation.
GQA-specific Q/KV head relationships could be lost and accidentally treated as MHA downstream.
Numeric or quantization materials may imply precision or tolerance changes that require approval before adoption.
Board/tool constraints may conflict with candidate templates, memory layout, bandwidth, or AXI/DDR assumptions.
Prepared design-space or template bounds may later influence tile size, parallelism, pipeline staging, memory layout, or data packing and therefore require human approval before final design use.
Input preparation does not satisfy checker-pass requirements; downstream checker evidence remains mandatory.

artifacts: SACG seed or prepared_inputs_summary in run directory
constraints: Preserve model semantics exactly from model_config and task_spec.
Do not treat grouped-query attention as multi-head attention; preserve distinct Q-head and KV-head counts.
Do not modify tests, golden outputs, tolerances, or checker behavior.
Do not claim design pass from input preparation alone; downstream checkers must validate all prepared artifacts.
Keep provenance, versions, and hashes for every imported material.
Board, AXI/DDR, memory capacity, clock, resource, and tool constraints must be captured without inventing unsupported capabilities.
Numeric and quantization inputs must be recorded as candidates or constraints, not silently adopted as unapproved semantic changes.
